decision.question: How do Notice, NoticeList and NoticeTray talk to each other in a View-style notification center?
decision.ask: How do Notice, NoticeList and NoticeTray talk to each other in a View-style notification center?

options.text: A. Parent owns the data (top-down). NoticeTray extends View and holds the array of notices; NoticeList extends View and only draws what it is handed; Notice extends View and draws one message. Tray: constructor({notices=[]}), render(){ this.bell = button.c('bell', '🔔').click(() => this.toggle()); this.list = new NoticeList({ notices: this.notices }); } · add(notice) pushes then this.list.add(notice) · dismiss(notice) splices then this.list.remove(notice) · toggle() flips .open and sets this.badge(). List: render(){ this.notices.forEach(n => this.add(n)); } · add(data){ const v = new Notice(data); this.append(v); return v; } · remove(v){ v.remove(); } · empty(). Notice: render(){ p(this.text); button.c('x','×').click(() => this.tray.dismiss(this)); } — it reaches up through a tray reference passed in. Everything calls methods on its child by direct reference.
options.say: A. Parent owns the data (top-down). NoticeTray extends View and holds the array of notices; NoticeList extends View and only draws what it is handed; Notice extends View and draws one message. Tray: constructor({notices=[]}), render(){ this.bell = button.c('bell', '🔔').click(() => this.toggle()); this.list = new NoticeList({ notices: this.notices }); } · add(notice) pushes then this.list.add(notice) · dismiss(notice) splices then this.list.remove(notice) · toggle() flips .open and sets this.badge(). List: render(){ this.notices.forEach(n => this.add(n)); } · add(data){ const v = new Notice(data); this.append(v); return v; } · remove(v){ v.remove(); } · empty(). Notice: render(){ p(this.text); button.c('x','×').click(() => this.tray.dismiss(this)); } — it reaches up through a tray reference passed in. Everything calls methods on its child by direct reference.
caveats: Notice must be handed a tray reference to dismiss itself, so it cannot be used outside a tray without a stub
Adding a second surface (a sidebar list, a toast) means the tray must know about it and call it too
options.caveat: Notice must be handed a tray reference to dismiss itself, so it cannot be used outside a tray without a stub Adding a second surface (a sidebar list, a toast) means the tray must know about it and call it too

options.text: B. The list is the source of truth and emits events (middle-out). NoticeList extends View, owns the array, and is an EventTarget-like emitter: add(data) makes a Notice, appends it, emits 'add'; remove(notice) splices, calls notice.remove(), emits 'remove'; unread() counts. Notice extends View: render(){ p(this.text); button.c('x','×').click(() => this.list.remove(this)); } · read() marks itself .read and emits 'read' through its list. NoticeTray extends View and is only the bell plus a box: constructor({list}), render(){ this.bell = button.c('bell').click(() => this.toggle()); this.drop = div.c('drop', () => this.list.appendTo(...)); } and this.list.on('add remove read', () => this.badge(this.list.unread())). Tray never changes data; it asks the list and redraws its badge. Any other surface listens to the same list.
options.say: B. The list is the source of truth and emits events (middle-out). NoticeList extends View, owns the array, and is an EventTarget-like emitter: add(data) makes a Notice, appends it, emits 'add'; remove(notice) splices, calls notice.remove(), emits 'remove'; unread() counts. Notice extends View: render(){ p(this.text); button.c('x','×').click(() => this.list.remove(this)); } · read() marks itself .read and emits 'read' through its list. NoticeTray extends View and is only the bell plus a box: constructor({list}), render(){ this.bell = button.c('bell').click(() => this.toggle()); this.drop = div.c('drop', () => this.list.appendTo(...)); } and this.list.on('add remove read', () => this.badge(this.list.unread())). Tray never changes data; it asks the list and redraws its badge. Any other surface listens to the same list.
caveats: A small emit/on seam has to be written on the list (or View gets one), which is one more thing to learn
Two listeners can both react to the same event and double-draw if someone forgets the list already drew the Notice
options.caveat: A small emit/on seam has to be written on the list (or View gets one), which is one more thing to learn Two listeners can both react to the same event and double-draw if someone forgets the list already drew the Notice

options.text: C. Every class is self-contained and talks only through the DOM (bottom-up). Notice extends View renders itself and, on its × button, dispatches a bubbling CustomEvent 'notice:dismiss' on its own element. NoticeList extends View: add(data) appends new Notice(data); on('notice:dismiss', e => e.target.view.remove()); count() reads this.el.children.length. NoticeTray extends View: renders the bell, appends a NoticeList, and listens for the same bubbling event (and 'notice:add') to update its badge from this.list.count(). No class holds a reference to another beyond parent→child append; the DOM tree is the only wiring.
options.say: C. Every class is self-contained and talks only through the DOM (bottom-up). Notice extends View renders itself and, on its × button, dispatches a bubbling CustomEvent 'notice:dismiss' on its own element. NoticeList extends View: add(data) appends new Notice(data); on('notice:dismiss', e => e.target.view.remove()); count() reads this.el.children.length. NoticeTray extends View: renders the bell, appends a NoticeList, and listens for the same bubbling event (and 'notice:add') to update its badge from this.list.count(). No class holds a reference to another beyond parent→child append; the DOM tree is the only wiring.
caveats: State lives in the DOM, so counting unread means reading classes off elements; nothing can be asked while the tray is not rendered
Bubbling events are invisible in code: a reader has to search the event name to find who listens, which fights 'clear beats brief'
options.caveat: State lives in the DOM, so counting unread means reading classes off elements; nothing can be asked while the tray is not rendered Bubbling events are invisible in code: a reader has to search the event name to find who listens, which fights 'clear beats brief'

decision.why: B keeps one owner of the data (the list) and lets the tray, a toast, or a sidebar all draw from it without the tray having to know them. Every method is still a plain chainable call on a View subclass (no virtual DOM, no reactivity): the list simply tells listeners that it changed. A is simpler for one tray but ties Notice to the tray; C hides the wiring in event names. If B costs too much, fall back to A.

decision.ask: Does the emit/on seam live on View itself or only on NoticeList?

options.text: Only NoticeList gets emit()/on(): a tiny Map of name to handlers, about ten lines
options.say: Only NoticeList gets emit()/on(): a tiny Map of name to handlers, about ten lines
caveats: A second list-like class would copy the ten lines
options.caveat: A second list-like class would copy the ten lines

options.text: View itself gets emit()/on() so every View can be listened to
options.say: View itself gets emit()/on() so every View can be listened to
caveats: Changes the core class for one feature; needs an ask first (core API)
options.caveat: Changes the core class for one feature; needs an ask first (core API)

decision.why: Keep core untouched; promote the seam to View only once a second class needs it (one of everything, built when needed).

decision.ask: What are the event names and payloads?

options.text: add, remove, read — the payload is the Notice view
options.say: add, remove, read — the payload is the Notice view

options.caveat: Short names can clash with DOM-sounding words in a reader head

options.text: notice:add, notice:remove, notice:read — payload the Notice view
options.say: notice:add, notice:remove, notice:read — payload the Notice view
caveats: Longer to type for no gain while only the list emits
options.caveat: Longer to type for no gain while only the list emits

decision.why: The list is the only emitter, so plain verbs read clearest; the payload is the Notice view, so a listener can call its methods.
